why: Frontiers 2021 review whose page 1 sets a 7 pt sidebar of editors, dates, and licence (x 45–159) beside the abstract and introduction (from x 176), with no gutter of its own on that page. Pins the first-page margin column: it is read apart from the page's other text and dropped with the front matter, so the whole abstract (its own superscripts, N^6 and m^6A, included) survives and INTRODUCTION opens the body. The title's raised 6 sits between title-size runs, so it stays in the title as a superscript (N^6-Methyladenosine). Its running footer's centred page number joins the footer's left half on some pages and its right half on others; compared cell by cell, the footer drops on every page, so the two-column reference list keeps its column edges and reads its 139 entries (Crossref lists 139) apart. The end matter after the last entry opens at bold labels that pdf.js splits around a regular-font ligature and apostrophe (`Con` · `fl` · `ict of Interest:`, `Publisher` · `’` · `s Note:`); each label reads whole, so the list ends at [139] and the end matter is back matter. A bold subsection heading whose `fi` ligature (or en dash) is set in a regular font stays a bold line, so `RNA m^6A Modification Modulates Phase Separation` reads whole over its two lines. Its siblings opening `m^6A Acts as a “…”` read whole too: their curly quotes, set in the regular face, hug the bold word they quote, and a heading may open with a lower-case symbol. Headings keep their superscripts. TABLE 1 spans both columns in 7 pt type with no cell crossing the gutter; it reads in four columns with all nine Ref entries, its wrapped lines standing as rows of their own.
